neighbours.label: a plural or paired subject about to be contrasted ('they are different', 'the two teams use different ...'), predicting different/separately
fire: The sisters share a bedroom, but they are different in almost every way.
The two hospitals use different rules for visiting hours.
Both teams want the trophy, and they have two very different strategies.
Our two offices handle billing differently, so invoices look different.
The brothers grew up together, yet they are different in their politics.
The two schools teach reading with different methods.
Both cities tax property, but they do it in different ways.
The twins sleep in one room, but they are different in their habits.
quiet: The sister shares a bedroom with her cousin during the holidays.
The hospital opens its visiting hours at noon on Sundays.
The team wants the trophy and trains every morning before work.
Our office handles billing on the first day of each month.
The brother grew up on a farm and still keeps a few goats.
The school teaches reading in small groups after lunch.
The city taxes property at a flat rate every year.
The child sleeps in a small room at the back of the house.

predictions: contrasted plural subjects 0.15-0.3; singular subjects without a contrast near 0.03
notes: Card: weak (max 14), ' they', ' two', ' by' before differ-words; logit effect promotes separately/different/both. Probe: 'they are different in' 0.288, 'they have two ways' 0.250, 'two labs used different methods' 0.194, 'different countries ... see' 0.167; singular controls 0.011-0.048.
